npcs.name: Magister Quen
npcs.description: Magister holds down a narrow tower with copper gutters with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Before dawn touches the roofs, Magister is already at a narrow tower with copper gutters, working as a town mage with flour, ink, sweat, or steel still on his fingers from yesterday. The habit everyone notices is simple: he answers practical questions with theory first. Close by sits his prized focus crystal cracked and still used, a small anchor in a loud town. Watched by Caldus; trades with Pire; buys from Vela. He wants to stabilize a ward that could spare the town another flood fire. He fears a temple-led ban on private laboratories more than open confrontation. A usable adventure hook trails him: Ordered a restricted treatise through Vela the same week Caldus copied a matching page.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; answers practical questions with theory first.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to stabilize a ward that could spare the town another flood fire.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around: Ordered a restricted treatise through Vela the same week Caldus copied a matching page.
npcs.rumor: The focus crystal cracked and still used once belonged to a person who vanished upriver.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the focus crystal cracked and still used.

relationships.note: Collects evidence of unsafe private magic.

npcs.name: Hala Quill
npcs.description: Hala holds down a public writing desk by the fountain with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Before dawn touches the roofs, Hala is already at a public writing desk by the fountain, working as a public scribe with flour, ink, sweat, or steel still on her fingers from yesterday. The habit everyone notices is simple: she offers fair rates and unfair honesty. Close by sits her prized traveling inkwell on a chain, a small anchor in a loud town. Honest counterpoint to Orin; helps Penna overflow work. She wants to open a small school for girls' letters. She fears being forced to copy forgeries more than open confrontation. A usable adventure hook trails her: Refused Pale Orin's request to 'borrow' her official nib cut.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; offers fair rates and unfair honesty.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to open a small school for girls' letters.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around: Refused Pale Orin's request to 'borrow' her official nib cut.
npcs.rumor: A smugglers' mark was seen near a public writing desk by the fountain on a night Hala worked late.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the traveling inkwell on a chain.

npcs.name: Vonn Dustmere
npcs.description: Vonn holds down the town library stacks with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Walk into the town library stacks and you will find Vonn Dustmere before you find a free chair. A 63-year-old Human library archivist, Vonn greets trouble the way other folk greet weather: with a coat and a plan. He dusts spines like soothing animals. The catalog cards in three conflicting systems travels with him almost everywhere. Works near Vela's rare shelf; aids Olda. His ambition is to finish a single coherent index before he dies. His nightmare is damp destroying the flood-year records. Right now, Found a missing chronicle volume returned with mill chalk on the cover.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; dusts spines like soothing animals.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to finish a single coherent index before he dies.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around: Found a missing chronicle volume returned with mill chalk on the cover.
npcs.rumor: Someone paid Vonn to forget a name connected to the town library stacks.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the catalog cards in three conflicting systems.

npcs.name: Pire Saltglass
npcs.description: Familiar face at a fume-stained shop with open windows; useful, stubborn, and hard to surprise.
npcs.biography: Before dawn touches the roofs, Pire is already at a fume-stained shop with open windows, working as a alchemist with flour, ink, sweat, or steel still on his fingers from yesterday. The habit everyone notices is simple: he labels explosions as 'educational'. Close by sits his prized goggles with one lens tinted rose, a small anchor in a loud town. Colleague to Quen; evidence path to Nedda. He wants to invent a safe lamp oil that smugglers can't dilute. He fears Quen's ward drawing lightning to the street more than open confrontation. A usable adventure hook trails him: Tested a sample from Nedda's 'grain' and found lamp oil cut with pitch.
npcs.personality: Proud of competence more than praise; labels explosions as 'educational'.
npcs.motivation: Protect his place at a fume-stained shop with open windows long enough to invent a safe lamp oil that smugglers can't dilute.
npcs.secret: Has not told allies that tested a sample from Nedda's 'grain' and found lamp oil cut with pitch.
npcs.rumor: Pire can open doors at a fume-stained shop with open windows after hours—if asked the right way.
npcs.voice: Measured gnome cadence; concrete nouns before adjectives.
npcs.appearance: Work-worn gnome garb; goggles with one lens tinted rose always nearby.

npcs.name: Essa Brightlane
npcs.description: Essa holds down manor schoolrooms and kitchen tables with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Some townsfolk swear Essa was born mid-shift at manor schoolrooms and kitchen tables; the truth is only slightly less devoted. This Half-Elf children's tutor, now 36, treats competence like courtesy. She turns chores into lessons, never far from the slate of multiplication dragons. Tutors Perrin; friend to Hala. Ask what she wants and she names it plainly: teach commoner children beside noble ones. Ask what she dreads and the answer is Perrin learning only pride. Then comes the fresh problem—Caught Perrin forging a practice excuse in her handwriting.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; turns chores into lessons.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to teach commoner children beside noble ones.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around: Caught Perrin forging a practice excuse in her handwriting.
npcs.rumor: Essa can open doors at manor schoolrooms and kitchen tables after hours—if asked the right way.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the slate of multiplication dragons.

npcs.name: Nym Fairchart
npcs.description: A cartographer rooted at survey posts outside the walls, known for how they humming while measuring angles.
npcs.biography: People looking for a reliable cartographer are sent to Nym, who claims survey posts outside the walls as home ground. At 42, this Human has learned to watch hands before faces. They humming while measuring angles; neighbors joke that they would miss a coronation before misplacing the case of chalk sticks in coded colors. Marks confused Sol; maps desired by Mouse and Jor. They is saving courage and coin alike to publish a public town map that settles property fights, while trying not to let their maps being used for invasion or crime decide the ending. Chalk marks in the cloister matched a survey line aimed at the old mill.
npcs.personality: Steady and sharp-eyed; humming while measuring angles.
npcs.motivation: To publish a public town map that settles property fights without feeding their maps being used for invasion or crime.
npcs.secret: Knows more about this than they admits: Chalk marks in the cloister matched a survey line aimed at the old mill.
npcs.rumor: The case of chalk sticks in coded colors once belonged to a person who vanished upriver.
npcs.voice: Low and practical, with a habit of repeating the important clause once.
npcs.appearance: A human silhouette framed by survey posts outside the walls, hands seldom empty of the case of chalk sticks in coded colors.

npcs.name: Olda Runebridge
npcs.description: The town historian people recommend when they actually want the job finished.
npcs.biography: Olda Runebridge keeps stone benches and foundation corners running with the stubborn patience of a 155-year-old Dwarf who has already survived worse seasons than this one. She rubs inscriptions with reverent thumbs, and the rubbing charcoal and rice paper is usually within reach when tempers rise. Works with Vonn; theory supports Mouse's maps. Her private aim is plain enough: prove the mill sits on a sealed undercroft. Still, she flinches at the thought of new money paving over old truths. Lately the trouble under her nose is this: Her rubbing of a foundation stone shows a tunnel arch 'filled by order'.
npcs.personality: Soft-spoken until principles are poked; rubs inscriptions with reverent thumbs.
npcs.motivation: Turn today's scrapes into tomorrow's chance to prove the mill sits on a sealed undercroft.
npcs.secret: Night thoughts keep returning to new money paving over old truths, especially since: Her rubbing of a foundation stone shows a tunnel arch 'filled by order'.
npcs.rumor: The rubbing charcoal and rice paper once belonged to a person who vanished upriver.
npcs.voice: Quick river-town diction, then sudden silences that mean more than words.
npcs.appearance: Easy to spot near stone benches and foundation corners: dwarf, practical layers, and that rubbing charcoal and rice paper.
